paragraphs: This paper studies how much a very small attention architecture can represent. It establishes universal approximation results for a single attention layer with a single head and limited supporting structure. The central idea is to interpret attention as a mechanism that divides an input domain into regions and assigns different values to those regions.

The authors construct attention weights so that these regional assignments imitate a target function. For self-attention, their construction places sum-of-linear transformations before the attention layer. With this setup, they prove that any continuous function on a compact domain can be approximated in the uniform norm, which measures the largest approximation error across the domain.

They also extend the construction to Lebesgue integrable functions under finite Lp norms and establish corresponding guarantees for single-head cross-attention. These are mathematical statements about representational capability with the stated attached structures. Their significance is that universal approximation can already arise in a narrowly configured attention mechanism through carefully engineered partitioning.
neurips-2025-attention-mechanism-max-aff.tldr: A single attention head with minimal supporting transformations can achieve universal approximation through a constructive partitioning of the input domain.

paragraphs: The paper introduces a version of the ski rental problem involving multiple items that can be rented or bought separately or together. At each step, the decision-maker must choose what to rent or purchase without knowing how long demand will continue. Purchases are irreversible, so decisions must balance immediate rental costs against the potential value of ownership.

The authors propose Sorted Optimal Amortized Cost, or SOAC, a randomized online algorithm with an optimal competitive ratio. This provides a formal guarantee for decisions made without knowing the future. The same approach can be extended to several established variants, including settings with multiple shops, multiple commodities, different purchasing options, and upgrades.

Building on SOAC, the paper develops an algorithm that incorporates machine-learned predictions to improve decisions. It can recover or improve existing learning-augmented results for classic and multi-shop ski rental. Experiments support the theoretical analysis and show advantages over the tested baselines, connecting the general combinatorial formulation to practical decision procedures.
neurips-2025-combinatorial-ski-rental-pr.tldr: SOAC provides optimal competitive guarantees for combinatorial rent-or-buy decisions and supports an extension that benefits from learned predictions.

paragraphs: ComRank addresses learning when an example can have several correct labels, but annotations identify labels that do not apply. These complementary labels provide indirect supervision: they tell the model which answers to avoid. Existing approaches often assume that irrelevant labels are selected uniformly, an assumption that can fail when annotation choices depend on the particular example.

The proposed framework learns a ranking instead. Its loss encourages known complementary labels to receive lower positions than labels that have not been marked complementary. This creates pairwise relationships between labels and makes greater use of their interdependence. Crucially, a label that was not marked irrelevant is a comparison candidate rather than an explicitly supplied positive annotation.

The paper proves Bayes consistency for its surrogate loss in both uniform and biased cases. This gives theoretical support for the ranking objective under the cases analyzed, while experiments demonstrate effectiveness on multi-label complementary learning tasks. The contribution connects a more flexible treatment of annotation bias with an objective that directly models relationships among candidate labels.
neurips-2025-comrank-ranking-loss-for-mu.tldr: ComRank learns from irrelevant-label annotations by ranking them below other labels, with consistency guarantees covering uniform and biased cases.

paragraphs: This paper analyzes stochastic gradient descent with gradient clipping for convex optimization. Clipping limits the size of gradient updates, and the question here is whether this modification supports strong convergence guarantees under a generalized smoothness condition. The authors work with the condition called (L0, L1)-smoothness, rather than restricting the analysis to the standard L-smooth setting.

Their main result is a high-probability convergence rate for clipped SGD. The rate matches the familiar SGD rate under standard smoothness up to polylogarithmic factors and additional additive terms. Those qualifications are part of the result: the paper establishes a close theoretical comparison between the settings, rather than an identical bound with all terms unchanged.

The authors also introduce an adaptive SGD variant that uses clipping and achieves the same guarantee. Empirical experiments examine the theory and the algorithmic choices. Together, these contributions show that clipping can support provable convergence in the stated convex, generalized-smoothness setting, with both a standard stochastic method and an adaptive alternative covered by the analysis.
neurips-2025-convergence-of-clipped-sgd-.tldr: Clipped SGD and an adaptive variant achieve high-probability convergence guarantees for convex, generalized-smooth functions that closely match standard smooth-case rates.

paragraphs: DictPFL targets the cost of protecting gradient exchanges in federated learning. Keeping raw training data within each institution does not eliminate leakage through shared gradients. Homomorphic encryption can protect aggregation, but encrypting every gradient can be expensive. DictPFL reduces the amount of information that needs transmission while encrypting every gradient it does transmit.

Its first module decomposes model weights into a static dictionary and an updatable lookup table. The dictionary stays local, while the lookup table is encrypted and aggregated. Its second module uses encryption-aware pruning, with consistent masks guided by training history, to further reduce the number of encrypted parameters. These modules change the representation and communication requirements together.

In the reported experiments, communication costs fall by 402–748 times and training accelerates by 28–65 times relative to fully encrypted federated learning. The method also improves overhead and speed over selective-encryption approaches, with runtime within twice that of plaintext federated learning. These findings support the practicality of protecting all transmitted gradients through a substantially smaller encrypted workload.
neurips-2025-dictpfl-efficient-and-priva.tldr: DictPFL makes encrypted federated training substantially cheaper by keeping a static dictionary local and encrypting a pruned, updatable lookup table.

paragraphs: DroneAudioset addresses a practical obstacle to using sound in drone-based search and rescue: the drone itself produces intense noise that can mask evidence of human presence. Audio could complement vision when visibility is poor or people are occluded, but developing useful systems requires recordings that capture the actual acoustic conditions around operating drones.

The dataset contains 23.5 hours of annotated recordings spanning different drone types, throttle settings, microphone configurations, and environments. Its signal-to-noise ratios range from −57.2 dB to −2.5 dB, covering challenging conditions in which the desired sound is weaker than the noise. This variation supports evaluation across a range of recording setups rather than a single fixed configuration.

The contribution is a resource for developing and systematically testing noise suppression and human-presence classification methods. It also supports investigation of practical design choices, including microphone placement and processing that accounts for drone noise. By providing real acoustic recordings with broad variation, the dataset advances the evidence base needed to design drone audition systems.
neurips-2025-droneaudioset-an-audio-data.tldr: DroneAudioset provides 23.5 hours of annotated audio for studying human-presence detection amid severe drone noise.

paragraphs: Error Broadcast and Decorrelation, or EBD, addresses how a neural network assigns responsibility for output errors to its internal layers. It sends output errors directly to individual layers, avoiding the weight transport associated with backpropagation. The paper provides a mathematical basis for deciding how each layer should respond to this shared error signal.

That basis comes from a property of minimum mean square error estimation: an optimal estimator’s error is orthogonal to functions of its input. EBD uses this idea to define local losses that penalize correlations between layer activations and output errors. Each layer therefore receives an objective tied to the relationship between its activity and the network’s remaining mistakes.

The resulting mechanism leads to a three-factor learning rule and can be integrated with biologically plausible learning frameworks. Numerical experiments find performance competitive with or better than other error-broadcast methods on benchmark datasets. The work supports EBD as a principled alternative training framework, while its connection to natural learning is presented in terms of biological plausibility.
neurips-2025-error-broadcast-and-decorre.tldr: EBD trains layers using broadcast output errors and decorrelation objectives grounded in a property of optimal mean-square-error estimation.

paragraphs: This paper tackles the shortage of training signals for recognizing unfamiliar inputs when a model combines multiple data modalities. Without examples of unknown data, models can make overconfident predictions on inputs outside their training distribution. The authors focus on both identifying such inputs and locating unfamiliar content through segmentation.

Their method, Feature Mixing, synthesizes multimodal outliers in feature space. It is designed to be simple, fast, and applicable across different modality combinations, with theoretical support for the synthesis approach. The generated outliers can also be further optimized to help the model separate familiar data from unfamiliar data, supplying supervision for a distinction that ordinary training examples do not directly provide.

The paper additionally introduces CARLA-OOD, a multimodal segmentation dataset containing synthetic unfamiliar objects across varied scenes and weather. Experiments on SemanticKITTI, nuScenes, CARLA-OOD, and MultiOOD report state-of-the-art performance and speedups of 10–370 times. These results support efficient outlier synthesis as a useful component of multimodal detection and segmentation in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-extremely-simple-multimodal.tldr: Feature Mixing efficiently synthesizes multimodal outliers to improve unfamiliar-input detection and segmentation, alongside a new CARLA-OOD dataset.

paragraphs: FedSVD addresses a tension between efficient fine-tuning and differential privacy in federated learning. LoRA represents a model update as the product of two small trainable matrices, B and A. When DP-SGD adds noise to gradients, this multiplication can amplify the disturbance. Fixing one matrix reduces noise but also limits how the model can adapt.

The method separates local optimization from global reparameterization. Each client trains and sends only B. The server aggregates these matrices, multiplies the result by the previous A, and uses singular value decomposition to factor the combined update again. The new A contains orthonormal right singular vectors, allowing its directions to adapt between rounds without clients directly optimizing both factors.

The analysis shows that this procedure avoids quadratic noise amplification and that A’s orthonormal structure bounds B’s gradient norms, preserving more useful signal under DP-SGD. Experiments report improved stability and performance across privacy settings and benchmarks, including non-private training. The key contribution is an adaptive factorization that combines restricted local updates with globally refreshed directions.
neurips-2025-fedsvd-adaptive-orthogonali.tldr: FedSVD refreshes LoRA factors through server-side SVD to reduce privacy-noise amplification while retaining adaptive update directions.

paragraphs: FHGS addresses a mismatch in using 3D Gaussian Splatting for scene understanding. A scene’s rendered appearance can depend on viewing direction, while its semantic features should remain consistent across views. Existing representations do not adequately reconcile these requirements, leading to features that change too much when the same scene is observed from different viewpoints.

The framework distills frozen, pretrained 2D features into sparse 3D structures while preserving real-time rendering. Its fusion architecture accommodates semantic features from models such as SAM and CLIP. A non-differentiable fusion mechanism encourages viewpoint-independent feature distributions, separating the consistency required for semantics from the directional behavior used to render appearance.

An optimization strategy inspired by electric potential fields combines external semantic supervision with internal guidance from primitive clustering. This supports both overall semantic alignment and local structural consistency. Benchmark comparisons report better feature fusion, noise suppression, and geometric precision, together with lower training time. The resulting representation offers practical advances for applications including semantic mapping, 3D stylization, and vision-language navigation.
neurips-2025-fhgs-feature-homogenized-ga.tldr: FHGS embeds pretrained semantic features into Gaussian scenes with greater cross-view consistency while preserving efficient rendering.

paragraphs: InfiGFusion aims to combine language models with different strengths into one model while retaining efficient inference. Existing logit-based methods compare vocabulary outputs dimension by dimension. This can overlook relationships between token types, including which tokens activate together across a sequence. The paper treats those relationships as useful structure for aligning models with different generation behaviors.

Its Graph-on-Logits Distillation loss retains the highest-scoring k logits at each output position and aggregates their outer products across the sequence. The resulting graph uses vocabulary channels as nodes and joint activations as edges. To compare this structure efficiently, the authors develop a sorting-based approximation to Gromov-Wasserstein distance, reducing the stated cost from O(n⁴) to O(n log n), with approximation guarantees.

Experiments report consistent improvements in fusion quality and stability, with stronger results than the compared models and fusion baselines across 11 reasoning, coding, and mathematics benchmarks. Reported gains over SFT include 35.6 on Multistep Arithmetic and 37.06 on Causal Judgement. These results support preserving relationships among outputs as a useful ingredient in model fusion.
neurips-2025-infigfusion-graph-on-logits.tldr: InfiGFusion improves language-model fusion by distilling token co-activation graphs with an efficient, theoretically supported structural comparison.

paragraphs: This paper introduces the task of detecting whether one model was distilled from a particular teacher. The setting reflects a specific access pattern: the suspected student’s weights are available, but the teacher can only be queried through an API. The motivation is model provenance, including concerns about replication through knowledge distillation.

The proposed framework combines data-free input synthesis with statistical score computation. It generates inputs for the detection process and uses computed scores to assess the possible teacher–student relationship. The framework is model-agnostic and applies to both classification and generation, giving the same broad detection strategy relevance across different kinds of model outputs.

Experiments cover diverse architectures for image classification and text-to-image generation. The authors report detection-accuracy improvements over their strongest baselines of 59.6% on CIFAR-10, 71.2% on ImageNet, and 20.0% for text-to-image generation. These findings provide empirical support for investigating distillation provenance under the stated access constraints, extending the problem beyond classification to generative models as well.
neurips-2025-knowledge-distillation-dete.tldr: A data-free statistical framework detects possible teacher–student distillation relationships using student weights and teacher API access.

paragraphs: LawShift examines whether models that predict legal judgments can respond to changes in statutes. These models use available case information to predict outcomes, but statutory revisions can change how that information should be interpreted. The paper identifies a gap in existing work: leading models were neither designed nor evaluated specifically for this kind of legal change.

The authors introduce a benchmark dataset covering 31 fine-grained types of statutory revision. This creates a structured way to test adaptability across different changes, making legal updates an explicit part of evaluation. The benchmark’s contribution is to organize the problem so that model responses to revisions can be assessed systematically.

The study evaluates five representative state-of-the-art models and finds substantial limitations in their handling of legal updates. It also reports that model architecture plays a critical role in adaptability. These findings make the benchmark useful for studying which design choices help legal judgment prediction remain responsive to changing statutes, rather than evaluating predictive performance only within an unchanged legal setting.
neurips-2025-lawshift-benchmarking-legal.tldr: LawShift benchmarks legal judgment prediction across 31 statutory change types and finds substantial adaptability gaps in five leading models.

paragraphs: HACO learns to estimate contact across the surface of a hand from datasets containing interactions with objects, other hands, scenes, and bodies. The paper identifies two distinct imbalances in these data. Most hand regions are not touching anything, and the contacts that do occur are concentrated at fingertips. Both patterns make learning less common contacts difficult.

To address the first imbalance, balanced contact sampling creates multiple groups representing different contact statistics and samples from them. This gives contact and non-contact vertices fairer representation during learning. The method therefore changes which training information the model encounters, rather than relying only on the naturally uneven distribution of observations.

To address the spatial imbalance, a vertex-level class-balanced loss weights each vertex according to its contact frequency across the dataset. This makes the correction specific to location on the hand. Together, sampling and spatially varying loss weighting support effective dense contact estimation from large-scale imbalanced data, with the reported outcome addressing both the overall rarity of contact and its uneven spatial distribution.
neurips-2025-learning-dense-hand-contact.tldr: HACO combines balanced sampling and location-specific loss weights to learn hand contact despite rare contacts and fingertip-heavy data.

paragraphs: The paper reconstructs stochastic dynamics from measurements of a population at an initial and final time, together with prior knowledge about its motion. This is the Schrödinger bridge problem: finding the most likely evolution compatible with the observations and reference dynamics. The authors focus on systems whose motion includes non-gradient forces, a relevant feature of biological systems outside equilibrium.

They replace the commonly used Brownian reference with a multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process having a general drift matrix. An asymmetric matrix allows the reference process to describe non-equilibrium behavior. When the endpoint distributions are Gaussian, the authors derive explicit expressions that exactly characterize both the static and dynamic bridge solutions.

For general endpoint distributions, they introduce mvOU-OTFM, which uses flow and score matching to learn an approximate bridge without simulation. Experiments on synthetic problems and real single-cell data report higher accuracy and significantly faster training than competing methods. The contribution combines exact results for the Gaussian case with an efficient approximate learning method for a broader range of distributions.
neurips-2025-learning-non-equilibrium-di.tldr: The paper extends Schrödinger bridges to non-equilibrium reference dynamics, providing exact Gaussian solutions and a simulation-free approximation method.

paragraphs: LoRATv2 improves the efficiency of transformer-based object tracking while incorporating information across video frames. Standard attention becomes expensive as token counts grow. The framework uses frame-wise causal attention: tokens within a frame retain full self-attention, while dependencies between frames follow temporal order. Key-value caching reuses past embeddings to further reduce repeated computation.

This attention structure gives different streams unequal access to temporal information. LoRATv2 responds with stream-specific LoRA adapters, assigning separate small adaptation modules to the template and each search stream while freezing the main vision transformer. Each stream can therefore specialize for its role without updating the entire backbone.

Training proceeds in two phases, starting with one search frame and then progressively adding frames and their LoRA modules. This curriculum supports longer-term tracking while retaining training efficiency. Across multiple benchmarks, the authors report state-of-the-art tracking performance, substantially improved efficiency, and a better performance-to-FLOPs ratio than the compared trackers. The method links temporal reuse, specialized adaptation, and progressive training in one tracking framework.
neurips-2025-loratv2-enabling-low-cost-t.tldr: LoRATv2 combines causal frame attention, cached embeddings, and stream-specific LoRA adapters for efficient temporal object tracking.

paragraphs: MIND addresses the difficulty of extracting meshes from unsigned distance fields, which describe distance to a surface without assigning an inside or outside. Learned fields rarely reach exactly zero, complicating surface extraction. Converting them locally into signed fields can create holes or unwanted components, and the abstract identifies a deeper representational failure for non-manifold geometry.

The method treats the desired surface as an interface between spatial regions. It first constructs a local field distinguishing the two sides of manifold patches, then extends that information into a global field with multiple labels. Multiple region labels allow the representation to separate all sides of a non-manifold structure instead of forcing a single two-sided description.

MIND combines this global labeling with the original distance field and extracts interfaces using a multi-labeled Marching Cubes algorithm. Experiments cover fields from point-cloud reconstruction, multi-view reconstruction, and medial axis transforms. The authors report robust handling of complex non-manifold surfaces and substantial improvements over existing methods, supporting global spatial partitioning as a useful route from distance fields to meshes.
neurips-2025-mind-material-interface-gen.tldr: MIND extracts non-manifold meshes from unsigned distance fields by constructing globally labeled regions and recovering their interfaces.

paragraphs: Compact Gaussian Streaming, or ComGS, reduces the storage required for online free-viewpoint video reconstruction with 3D Gaussian Splatting. The paper argues that representing motion point by point misses an opportunity: neighboring points on a moving object often move consistently. ComGS uses a sparse set of keypoints to represent that shared motion more compactly.

A viewspace gradient difference strategy identifies motion-sensitive keypoints within moving regions. The method then predicts a spatial influence field that propagates each keypoint’s motion to neighboring Gaussian points with similar movement. Transmitting keypoint attributes provides a smaller representation of the scene’s motion. An error-aware correction mechanism selectively refines inaccurate regions during key-frame reconstruction to reduce accumulated errors.

The reported results show storage reductions of over 159 times relative to 3DGStream and 14 times relative to QUEEN, while retaining competitive visual fidelity and rendering speed. These findings support exploiting local motion consistency as a way to compress dynamic Gaussian representations without giving up the responsiveness sought in free-viewpoint video.
neurips-2025-motion-matters-compact-gaus.tldr: ComGS represents shared Gaussian-point motion through sparse keypoints, sharply reducing video storage while maintaining competitive rendering quality and speed.

paragraphs: Reduced-order models speed up simulations by representing a large physical system in a compact latent space. The paper identifies a mismatch in conventional training: numerical solvers generate the data, but their governing physics is then excluded from learning. As a result, learned dynamics can drift from the discretized equations, limiting forecasts and generalization.

Phi-ROM brings differentiable PDE solvers into the training process. The solver directly shapes both the latent dynamics and their dependence on physical parameters, strengthening correspondence between the reduced representation and the full system. This connects the compact model’s evolution to the numerical physics that generated the solution fields.

The authors report improvements over data-driven reduced-order models and other physics-informed approaches, including generalization to unseen parameters, forecasts beyond the training horizon, continuity in space and time, and reduced data requirements. The framework also reconstructs and forecasts fields from sparse, irregular observations. Demonstrations across several solvers and an extensible JAX implementation support its use as a flexible framework for reconstruction, forecasting, and data assimilation.
neurips-2025-physics-informed-reduced-or.tldr: Phi-ROM trains compact dynamical models through differentiable PDE solvers to improve physical consistency, generalization, and long-term forecasting.

paragraphs: This paper studies constrained optimization where the objective sums a quasi-self-concordant function over n linear residuals in d variables, with n at least d. Its main algorithm uses a trust-region method. The computational focus is the oracle used within that method, whose implementation requires approximately d to the one-third power linear-system solves, suppressing logarithmic factors.

That improves an earlier dependence on n to the one-third power. The distinction matters for overdetermined problems, where the number of residuals can exceed the number of variables. The new oracle relies on constrained infinity-norm regression, which minimizes the largest absolute residual while respecting the linear equality constraints.

For this regression problem, the authors give a (1+epsilon)-approximation algorithm requiring O((d^(1/3)/epsilon + 1/epsilon²) log(n/epsilon)) linear-system solves. It combines infinity-norm Lewis weight overestimates with an iteratively reweighted least-squares approach. Experiments report substantially better runtime than the standard CVX solver. The contribution therefore includes both a sharper theoretical oracle implementation and empirical evidence for its computational usefulness.
neurips-2025-quasi-self-concordant-optim.tldr: A Lewis-weight-based regression algorithm improves the linear-system-solve complexity of an oracle for constrained quasi-self-concordant optimization.

paragraphs: RedOUT detects graphs that differ from the distribution a classifier encountered during training. The paper focuses on structural redundancy, which can distort the semantic information represented by a graph and weaken unfamiliar-input detection. Its approach operates at test time and uses an unsupervised framework, making the treatment of redundant structure central to the detection process.

The authors introduce a Redundancy-aware Graph Information Bottleneck that separates the objective into essential information and irrelevant redundancy. They reduce the redundancy component by minimizing structural entropy. The paper also derives upper and lower bounds to support optimization, providing theoretical grounding for how the framework handles the separated information components.

Experiments on real-world datasets report superior detection performance, with an average improvement of 6.7% and a 17.3% improvement over the best competitor on the ClinTox/LIPO dataset pair. These results support the idea that graph OOD detection benefits from explicitly addressing irrelevant structural information. The contribution joins a redundancy-focused objective with a test-time procedure for distinguishing familiar and unfamiliar graphs.
neurips-2025-redundancy-aware-test-time-.tldr: RedOUT improves test-time graph OOD detection by separating useful information from structural redundancy and reducing the latter through structural entropy.

paragraphs: RoLoRA studies how to fine-tune language models efficiently across federated participants using LoRA adapters. LoRA reduces computation and communication by learning small projection matrices. The paper emphasizes that both the down-projection and up-projection matrices matter for expressiveness and robustness, motivating a training method that preserves learning in both parts of the adapter.

The proposed framework uses alternating optimization for these matrices. Its analysis begins with a linear model to explain why learning both projections is important. The authors validate those insights on a nonlinear model and separately establish convergence under general conditions. This separates the argument about representational benefits from the proof governing optimization behavior.

Experiments include RoBERTa-Large and Llama-2-7B across diverse tasks and federated settings. The authors report advantages over prior methods that produce imperfect model updates or constrain expressiveness. Together, the theoretical and empirical results support alternating optimization as a way to retain the benefits of both LoRA factors while addressing the demands of federated fine-tuning.
neurips-2025-robust-federated-finetuning.tldr: RoLoRA alternates optimization of both LoRA projection matrices to improve expressiveness and robustness in federated language-model fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Performative prediction studies situations where deploying a model changes the data it will later encounter. Repeated retraining can therefore alter its own learning environment. This paper investigates convergence to a stable point, where deployment no longer changes the data distribution, and asks whether retaining data from earlier retraining rounds can improve that process.

The authors extend Repeated Risk Minimization into a class called Affine Risk Minimizers, which uses historical datasets from previous snapshots. This broader class converges for a wider collection of problems. They also derive a new upper bound for methods using only the latest dataset and prove tightness of that bound and earlier bounds within the same regime.

The new class can surpass the lower bound applying to standard Repeated Risk Minimization, showing the benefit of expanding the algorithm’s access to history. Experiments observe faster convergence on performative prediction benchmarks. Additional lower-bound analysis within the affine framework quantifies potential speed improvements, connecting the proposed methods to formal limits on what such retraining schemes can achieve.
neurips-2025-tight-lower-bounds-and-impr.tldr: Using historical retraining data broadens convergence guarantees in performative prediction and can outperform limits that apply to standard repeated risk minimization.

paragraphs: VDRP tackles human-object interaction detection when particular verb-object combinations were absent during training. The model must locate people and objects and identify their interaction. Two visual challenges complicate this: the same verb can appear in different poses and contexts, while different verbs can produce similar-looking interactions.

The framework adapts prompts for a pretrained vision-language model using information about visual diversity. It injects group-wise visual variance into the prompt’s context representation and adds Gaussian perturbations to encourage coverage of different appearances of a verb. This makes the prompt-learning process explicitly account for variation within an interaction class.

A second component retrieves concepts from the human region, object region, and their combined region. These concepts augment the diversity-aware prompts to improve distinctions among verbs using localized evidence. On HICO-DET, the authors report state-of-the-art results under four zero-shot settings. The findings support combining variation-aware prompts with region-specific information to address both diverse appearances within a class and visual overlap between classes.
neurips-2025-visual-diversity-and-region.tldr: VDRP combines visually diverse prompt representations with region-specific concepts to improve recognition of unseen human-object interaction combinations.

paragraphs: WebThinker addresses the limits of reasoning models that rely on knowledge stored during training. Complex research tasks can require information from multiple web sources, together with sustained reasoning and report writing. The paper turns these activities into parts of an autonomous research process that can seek new information as knowledge gaps emerge.

Its Deep Web Explorer module enables searching, navigating pages, and extracting information during reasoning. An Autonomous Think-Search-and-Draft strategy interleaves those actions with report composition, allowing information gathering and writing to develop together. The authors further train research-tool use through iterative online Direct Preference Optimization, presented as an RL-based training strategy.

Experiments cover GPQA, GAIA, WebWalkerQA, and HLE reasoning benchmarks, as well as scientific report generation on Glaive. The authors report significant improvements over existing methods and strong proprietary systems. These results support integrating research tools into the reasoning process and training their use, with the stated benefit of greater reliability and applicability on complex, knowledge-intensive tasks.
neurips-2025-webthinker-empowering-large.tldr: WebThinker equips reasoning models to interleave web exploration, reasoning, and report drafting, with training that improves research-tool use.
